name: innovation-ai
title: Innovation – AI use cases
description: The use-case method of the digitalswitzerland AI playbook (docs/04): assessment sections and fields with the impact score and the feasibility index, the project statuses and templates AI use case (gates G0–G3 with the playbook checklists) and AI ambition, the groups Innovation team, Review board and Compliance, assignment roles, saved views, workshop map templates and the prioritization matrix.

group:innovation_team.name: Innovation team
group:innovation_team.description: Moderates ideation workshops, matures ideas and manages the use-case projects (playbook p. 46).

group:review_board.name: Review board
group:review_board.description: Senior stakeholders who decide on mature ideas and at the gates; they edit the section Review board decision (p. 46).

group:compliance.name: Compliance
group:compliance.description: Approves ideas and use cases from the compliance side; edits the section Compliance approval (p. 46).

section:use_case_profile.name: Use case profile
section:use_case_profile.description: The structured description of the idea (playbook pp. 29–35).

section:value.name: Value
section:value.description: What the use case is worth, and the impact score (p. 34).

section:feasibility.name: Feasibility
section:feasibility.description: Twelve statements rated 0–5 and the time to a proof of value – the feasibility index, max. 65 (p. 34).

section:risk_responsibility.name: Risk & responsibility
section:risk_responsibility.description: Exceptional risks, EU AI Act class, data and human oversight (pp. 34, 64–69).

section:compliance_approval.name: Compliance approval
section:compliance_approval.description: Editable by the group Compliance only.

section:review_board_decision.name: Review board decision
section:review_board_decision.description: Editable by the group Review board only (p. 46).

section:data_platform.name: Data & platform
section:data_platform.description: Data sources, AI readiness, platform and integration (pp. 58–63).

section:charter.name: Charter
section:charter.description: Business contribution, scope, timeline and success criteria written down (p. 85).

section:ambition.name: Ambition
section:ambition.description: Goals and guiding principles for using AI (pp. 29–31).

field:problem.label: Addressed problem
field:problem.helpText: Which problem does the use case solve, for whom? (playbook p. 35)

field:data_basis.label: Required data basis
field:data_basis.helpText: Which data does the solution need, and where does it come from? (p. 35)

field:expected_output.label: Expected output
field:expected_output.helpText: What does the AI deliver – an answer, a draft, a decision, an action? (p. 35)

field:impact_field.label: Impact field
field:impact_field.helpText: Where the use case creates its impact (impact field, p. 29).

field:transformation_level.label: Transformation level
field:transformation_level.helpText: How far the use case changes the business (p. 87).

field:ambition_contribution.label: Contribution to the AI ambition
field:ambition_contribution.helpText: How does the use case contribute to the AI ambition and the strategy? (p. 34)

field:strategic_advantages.label: Strategic advantages
field:strategic_advantages.helpText: Counts in the impact score (up to 5).

options.label: Better quality of service or product

field:business_value_chf.label: Estimated business value
field:business_value_chf.helpText: Per year, with the assumptions below (p. 34).

field:impact_reach.label: Reach
field:impact_reach.helpText: How many people or processes are affected?

field:impact_strategic.label: Strategic fit
field:impact_strategic.helpText: How well does the use case fit the AI ambition?

field:impact_value_band.label: Value band
field:impact_value_band.helpText: Business value per year, as points for the impact score.

field:impact_score.label: Impact score
field:impact_score.helpText: Reach + strategic fit + value band + strategic advantages (up to 5), as 0–100. Y-axis of the prioritization matrix.

field:feas_data_access.label: We have access to the data
field:feas_data_access.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_infra.label: We have the infrastructure
field:feas_infra.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_data_quality.label: We have the data quality
field:feas_data_quality.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_solution_known.label: We know how to solve the problem
field:feas_solution_known.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_similar_built.label: A similar solution has been built before
field:feas_similar_built.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_technologies.label: We know suitable technologies
field:feas_technologies.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_no_new_processes.label: No new processes are needed
field:feas_no_new_processes.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_processes_adaptable.label: Existing processes are easy to adapt
field:feas_processes_adaptable.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_no_major_changes.label: No substantial changes are needed
field:feas_no_major_changes.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_tech_knowhow.label: Technical know-how is available
field:feas_tech_knowhow.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_domain_knowhow.label: Domain know-how is available
field:feas_domain_knowhow.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:feas_ai_understanding.label: General AI understanding is available
field:feas_ai_understanding.helpText: 0 = does not apply, 5 = fully applies; n/a if it can't be rated (p. 34).

field:time_to_proof_of_value.label: Time to a verified proof of value

field:feasibility_index.label: Feasibility index
field:feasibility_index.helpText: Sum of the 12 ratings and the time to proof of value (max. 65); n/a answers are left out and the result is scaled to 65. X-axis of the prioritization matrix.

field:risk_flags.label: Exceptional risks
field:risk_flags.helpText: Risks that need a deeper analysis (p. 34).

options.label: Human in the loop (e.g. black-swan events)

field:risk_analysis.label: Risk analysis
field:risk_analysis.helpText: Required when a risk is flagged above.

field:eu_ai_act_class.label: EU AI Act risk class
field:eu_ai_act_class.helpText: Risk class of the AI system (pp. 66–67).

field:is_ai_system.label: AI system
field:is_ai_system.helpText: An AI system in the sense of the EU AI Act – listed in the AI system inventory (p. 67).

field:data_classification.label: Data classification
field:data_classification.helpText: Highest classification of the data used (p. 58).

field:external_models_allowed.label: External models allowed
field:external_models_allowed.helpText: The data may go into external models (p. 58).

field:compliance_approved.label: Compliance approved
field:compliance_approved.helpText: Set by the group Compliance; required before the review board (p. 46).

field:data_sources.label: Data sources
field:data_sources.helpText: Internal and external sources, format, access, quality, gaps (p. 58).

field:strategic_relevance.label: Strategic relevance
field:strategic_relevance.helpText: A strategic differentiator speaks for make, a commodity for buy (p. 38).

field:speed_needed.label: Need for speed
field:speed_needed.helpText: How critical is the time to market?

field:can_operate.label: We can operate it ourselves
field:can_operate.helpText: Know-how and resources for long-term operation are available.

field:business_contribution.label: Business contribution
field:business_contribution.helpText: What the initiative contributes to the business (p. 85).

field:timebox_end.label: End of timebox
field:timebox_end.helpText: Experiments last 8–12 weeks at most (p. 40); overdue when passed.

field:adoption_pct.label: Adoption
field:adoption_pct.helpText: Share of the target group using the solution, e.g. 50 % (p. 75).

field:kpi_notes.label: KPIs
field:kpi_notes.helpText: Active users, usage frequency, time saved, cycle time, error rate, satisfaction (p. 79).

field:qualitative_goals.label: Qualitative goals
field:qualitative_goals.helpText: Structures to build, business impact, mobilising the organisation, a clear target picture (p. 30).

field:quantitative_targets.label: Quantitative targets
field:quantitative_targets.helpText: Goals with dates, e.g. "5 use cases tested" – one milestone per target.

template:ai_use_case.name: AI use case
template:ai_use_case.description: A use case selected by the review board, from the test to operation: prototype / PoC → MVP / pilot → rollout & scaling, with a gate after every stage and the playbook checklists as Definition of Done (playbook pp. 38–41).

milestones.title: Ready for test
milestones.description: The review board said go; key persons are named and the test phase is prepared (playbook step 5, p. 37).
dod: Key persons for the use case defined (sponsor, domain expert, delivery team)
Test phase prepared: scope, timebox and resources agreed
Charter written: business contribution, scope, responsibilities and timeline (section Charter)

milestones.title: Prototype built
milestones.description: Is the AI solution feasible and effective for the problem? (p. 38)
dod: Test concept written
Test data available
Evaluation criteria defined
Prototype built

milestones.title: PoC decision
milestones.description: Cancel, iterate or continue after the prototype; make or buy is decided before the MVP (pp. 38–41, 63).
dod: PoC goals, test cases, data and success criteria defined
PoC result documented and assessed
Go / no-go decided (or iterate)
Make or buy decided (section Make or buy)
Own data needed? A data platform considered
Data silos: a central repository considered
Modalities covered (structured, unstructured, text, image, audio, video)
Make or buy assessed against the available skills and resources
Data location and security considered
Models and token costs compared; total cost of ownership and scaling considered

milestones.title: MVP live with pilot group
milestones.description: Does the solution create real value in daily use, and can it be improved iteratively? (p. 38)
dod: Core features built
User interface built
Pilot group active
Feedback loops running; MVP improved from the feedback

milestones.title: Scale decision
milestones.description: Acceptance in the pilot is measured; data, responsible AI and security are checked before the rollout (pp. 41, 59, 65, 69).
dod: Acceptance in the pilot group measured
EU AI Act risk class set (section Risk & responsibility)
Data: the data used for the use case is treated as a strategic asset
Data: data strategy aligned with the business strategy and the core processes
Data: data management principles applied (ownership, quality process, master data)
Data: context data / ontologies for the use case defined
Data: "Is this dataset AI-ready?" answered – may it go into external models; PII, contracts and customer data handled; anonymisation / masking decided; legal / compliance sign-off before production
Responsible AI: data quality checked (current, high quality, representative)
Responsible AI: bias checks done
Responsible AI: ethical guidelines applied
Responsible AI: legal compliance ensured (data protection, EU AI Act, GDPR)
Responsible AI: AI decisions transparent and explainable for users
Responsible AI: personal data processed only with protection measures
Responsible AI: human control for critical decisions
Responsible AI: security and robustness tested (attacks, unexpected input)
Security: AI governance – rules, roles and responsibilities defined; business, IT, legal and security work together
Security: platform and model choice – providers, model quality, security, cost, data location and sovereignty assessed
Security: technical controls – guardrails, shadow-AI detection, approval process for new AI applications
Security: people – regular training on AI risks, open exchange, AI do's and don'ts communicated

milestones.title: Rolled out
milestones.description: How is the solution optimised, integrated and maintained long-term? (p. 38)
dod: Solution integrated into the target systems
Logging and monitoring set up
Incident and change process defined
Data and model governance in place
Target groups trained
Quick reference and user guides available
Support in place

milestones.title: Impact review
milestones.description: Impact and ROI are measured and reported; decide to continue, scale or retire (pp. 41, 79, 85).
dod: KPIs defined
Baseline vs after measured
Reporting and review rhythm fixed
Decision taken: continue, scale or retire
Enablement: AI skills built (trainings, peer learning, micro-learning)
Enablement: a culture of experimentation and of learning from errors supported
Enablement: core story on benefits and goals communicated, success stories shared
Enablement: end users involved early, feedback loops, quick wins
Enablement: roles and structures clear (champions, centre of enablement / excellence, support)
Enablement: adoption, usage and impact tracked with KPIs and pulse checks
Enablement: guardrails for privacy, fairness and responsible use set

template:ai_ambition.name: AI ambition
template:ai_ambition.description: Goals and guiding principles for using AI, the basis for every decision on use cases. Ideas and projects are linked to it with "contributes to" (playbook pp. 29–31).

fieldDefaults.field:guiding_principles:
- Start small, grow big
- End users are always in the driver's seat
- Share learnings systematically
- Anchor AI on all hierarchy levels
- Measure impact and acceptance continuously

milestones.title: Ambition defined
milestones.description: Written by a core team of management, senior leadership and IT (p. 31).
dod: Constraints from the strategy answered: what is non-negotiable?
Contribution of AI to the strategy described
Qualitative and quantitative ambition set: how is success defined?
Guiding principles agreed

milestones.title: Ideation round
milestones.description: Identify: define the focus of the search, collect and describe use-case ideas (pp. 32–33).
dod: AI ambition consulted and search focus defined
Contributors and core team defined
GenAI research and workshop carried out
At least 30 ideas generated
Ideas roughly documented

milestones.title: Portfolio review
milestones.description: Assess & prioritize: build the use-case portfolio and select the core ideas (pp. 34–37).
dod: Assessment template filled for every idea
Assessed ideas placed in the prioritization matrix
Quick wins and star initiatives examined; 2–3 core ideas selected
Key persons per core idea defined; test phase prepared

milestones.title: 5 use cases tested
milestones.description: Example target from the playbook (p. 30) – adapt the number and the date, or delete it.
dod: Five use cases tested as PoC, MVP or pilot

milestones.title: 50+ employees trained
milestones.description: Example target from the playbook (p. 30) – adapt or delete.
dod: At least 50 employees trained in using AI

milestones.title: 3 applications productive
milestones.description: Example target from the playbook (p. 30) – adapt or delete.
dod: Three applications in operation with at least 15 % efficiency gain

milestones.title: AI community established
milestones.description: Example target from the playbook (p. 30) – adapt or delete.
dod: An AI community established and meeting regularly

role:innovation_team.name: Innovation team
role:innovation_team.description: Moderates the workshops, matures the idea, manages the project.

role:review_board.name: Review board
role:review_board.description: Decides at the review board and at the gates.

role:domain_expert.name: Domain expert
role:domain_expert.description: Business person with domain expertise: makes sure the solution meets the business needs and judges the quality of the AI output.

role:delivery_team.name: Delivery team
role:delivery_team.description: Builds the solution: software, prompt engineering and GenAI skills.

role:sponsor.name: Sponsor
role:sponsor.description: Business owner who backs and funds the use case.

role:data_owner.name: Data owner
role:data_owner.description: Responsible for the data used: quality, sensitivity, approval for use in AI systems.

role:ai_champion.name: AI champion
role:ai_champion.description: Promotes adoption in the target group and is the first contact for its users.

view:review_board_agenda.name: Review board agenda
view:review_board_agenda.description: Ideas ready for the review board, highest impact first.

view:ai_system_inventory.name: AI system inventory
view:ai_system_inventory.description: All AI systems with their EU AI Act class – step 1 of the EU AI Act (p. 67).

view:running_experiments.name: Running experiments
view:running_experiments.description: Use cases in Prototype / PoC – experiments last 12 weeks at most (p. 40).

view:gate_decisions.name: Gate decisions
view:gate_decisions.description: The stop / go / scale record: decided gates of all projects, newest first (p. 85).

maptemplate:impact_field.name: Impact field canvas
maptemplate:impact_field.description: The 2×2 impact field of the playbook (p. 29): external ↔ internal × individual ↔ organisation. Sets the focus of the use-case search; ideas are created directly in their quadrant during the workshop.

elements.text: Where does the idea create its impact? Create every idea in its field (playbook p. 29).
How can GenAI strengthen customer loyalty?
What will our business model look like?
How can GenAI raise personal productivity?
How will GenAI redefine how we work?

maptemplate:crazy_8s.name: Crazy 8s
maptemplate:crazy_8s.description: Eight frames for the Crazy 8s creativity method – one copy per participant (p. 32).

elements.text: Eight ideas in eight minutes: sketch one idea per frame, one minute each – quantity over quality. Then present, cluster and vote (p. 32).

maptemplate:customer_journey.name: Customer journey
maptemplate:customer_journey.description: Swimlanes for customer journey mapping: stages × touchpoints, pain points and AI opportunities (p. 32).

elements.text: Follow the customer through every stage: where are the touchpoints and pain points, and where could AI help? Rename the stages as needed (p. 32).

maptemplate:use_case_funnel.name: Use-case funnel
maptemplate:use_case_funnel.description: One column per idea status – a manual board of the funnel for workshops and the review board.

elements.text: Move every idea card into the column of its status – from the long list (at least 30 ideas) to the 2–3 core ideas (pp. 31–37).

matrixpreset:prioritization.name: Prioritization matrix
matrixpreset:prioritization.description: Business impact × ease of implementation (playbook pp. 36–37). Start with the quick wins, build the star initiatives, keep the difficult but impactful ones in the pipeline and only observe the rest.
